thread:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing tail latency spikes on several prod inference nodes, looks like KV reclaim/evict activity lines up with the spikes.
Ryan: Where in the trace? any repro or logs we can look at quickly?
Maya: Quick excerpt from profiler around the spike window:
```
[2026-03-12T12:03:45Z] pager: reclaim_loop: duration=120ms evict_batch=256 reclaimed=0
[2026-03-12T12:03:45Z] kv_cache: reuse_hit=false slab_frag=0.42 lru_walk=350ms pinned_pages=512
[2026-03-12T12:03:45Z] runtime: batcher_concurrency=48 seq_len_p95=2048 kernel=small_gemm
```
Priya: Hmm that lru_walk=350ms stands out. Under sustained long contexts the LRU walker scanning hot/cold boundary can blow latency. FIFO might reduce walking cost but we've seen correctness challenges.
Tana: Correctness note — FIFO+reinsertion races caused ordering anomalies in the replay harness last quarter. We had to add a tombstone handshake to avoid duplicates.
Josh: I have a deterministic repro that toggles the race by flipping atomic semantics. With ENABLE_ATOMIC_SWAP=0 the reinsert order becomes non-deterministic.
Maya: Also saw kernel-selection shift (small_gemm) at the same time — likely more mini-ops per token -> more frequent KV touches -> paging churn.
Ryan: Makes sense. Batching heuristic increases concurrency to hit latency SLOs but that increases pinned working set. Two levers: reduce evict_batch and reduce batcher_concurrency. Which to try first?
Priya: Reduce evict_batch to 64 for a canary, run A/B lru vs fifo under identical load and run correctness checker (replay/trace diff).
Josh: I'll kick off the harness. Command I'm using:
```
./kv_repro --seed=42 --concurrency=64 --longctx=8192 --policy=lru --evict-batch=256 --trace=out.pb
```
Josh: swapping evict-batch=64 now, will run both policies back-to-back and upload traces.
KVWatcherBot: alert: kv_pager_pressure exceeded threshold on host-13, 2026-03-12T12:04:02Z
incident-bot: incident created: INC-2026-223 kv-pressure-tail-latency, paging cascade suspected
Ryan: Rolled a canary change to reduce evict_batch -> 64 on 3 nodes and capped batcher_concurrency at 32. Observed immediate tail latency drop ~18% on canary (p95->p99 window).
Maya: Nice, can we get a longer run (1h) and run the correctness replay to ensure no reinsert dupes under FIFO? Priya can coordinate.
Priya: I'll schedule the A/B runs and add a CI regression: run kv_repro with --policy=fifo and --policy=lru nightly and diff. Also adding an invariant check for duplicate keys in replayed sequence.
Tana: If FIFO passes correctness under the invariant, it might be a better default under heavy long-context workloads. But we should keep the atomic handshake available for edge customers.
Josh: Uploading canary traces to /opt/prof/kv/1727777777/ once done.
Maya: Thanks team. Action items: Ryan monitor canary 1h, Priya run A/B + CI tests, Josh upload traces & repro artifacts, Tana review correctness choke points. Will sync in #eng-runtime in 90m if issues persist. :thumbsup:
Ryan: Ack.
Priya: Ack, starting the A/B now.
KVWatcherBot: status: canary hosts stable at 2026-03-12T12:50:00Z — p99 latency down 16-20% vs baseline
Maya: Great signal. If canary holds we will promote the evict_batch reduction and look at a short-term batching-cap cap until we implement a smarter adaptive policy (workload-aware batcher + kernel-informed routing).
